# WebSocket and Realtime Platform

The Awtsmoos gives one transport many worlds without letting identity dissolve into message text;
Awtsmoos.com owns a realtime platform where registry, router, client state, and application contracts connect.

## Server architecture

Root HTTP infrastructure forwards upgrade requests to the dynamic server's WebSocket layer. `websocket/core/socketUpgrade.js` resolves trusted upgrade identity, applies Mission Room-specific admission policy when applicable, writes the handshake, attaches a client session, and then publishes connection activity.

Normal text messages enter `websocket/apps/messageRouter.js`, which delegates to one server-owned `RealtimePlatform`. That platform owns an `ApplicationRegistry`, an `ApplicationRouter`, and shared server state.

## Legacy and versioned protocols coexist

`ApplicationRouter` parses each complete UTF-8 JSON message. Legacy messages are routed through legacy compatibility logic. Versioned messages carry an application/version contract and are routed through the registered realtime application platform.

Trusted identity comes from `client.identity`, populated by the socket session. The ApplicationRouter explicitly keeps identity out of message-payload authority: a client message cannot simply supply its own trusted account identity.

## Important separate subsystems

- **Mission Rooms:** pre-handshake one-time ticket/origin/authority/protocol checks. See [MISSION_ROOMS.md](MISSION_ROOMS.md).
- **Tunnel Relay:** account-bound agent/device transport and request correlation. It is not one of the eight built-in versioned application factories. See [TUNNEL_RELAY.md](TUNNEL_RELAY.md).
- **Social/live compatibility:** page presence, social events, typing/reading state, live preview. See [APPLICATIONS.md](APPLICATIONS.md).
